subject: Weekly leadership roundup — priorities, QBR playbook, and blockers
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: leadership-distro@redwood.ai
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Weekly leadership roundup — priorities, QBR playbook, and blockers

Team —

Quick weekly for leadership ahead of the QBR dry run. Focused asks at the top, then a short win/risk recap so we can align the playbook before Friday.

Asks (high-priority)
- QBR playbook: please review slides 3–8 (owner: Marissa). Need sign-off on the escalation ladder and the fallback models by Wed COB.
- Ops cost variance: Karthik, can you confirm the Dedicated capacity variance and whether we should call this out in the financial appendix?
- Incident snapshot: Markus, please confirm the postmortem ETA for the multi-region KV cache incident. We need a short blurb for the risk register.

Wins (this week)
- Hosted API: 3% tail-latency improvement after kernel tweak; internal benchmark attached.
- Community: two new model contributions in the catalog that reduce small-doc latency on average.

Risks / Chokepoints
- SRE backlog: ongoing KV-cache regressions are the largest risk to our latency SLO for Dedicated (see attached SRE_incident_snapshot_Oct.csv).
- QBR readiness: the playbook still needs the escalation flow and the customer-facing slide explaining fallback behavior.

Logistics
- Dry run: Thu 10/15 10:00–11:30 PT (Zoom link in Drive). Please be prepared with 1 slide per owner for decisions.
- Deliverables: Marissa — deck draft (slides 1–12); Karthik — cost variance note; Markus — incident blurb.

Attachments: QBR_playbook_draft_v1.pptx (pptx, 4 slides stub), SRE_incident_snapshot_Oct.csv (csv, 1 sheet stub)

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Operations & Strategy
Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekly leadership roundup — priorities, QBR playbook, and blockers

Laura —

Quick clarifications:
1) Dedicated variance: the majority of the delta is a one-off out-of-cycle provisioning charge for a proof-of-concept customer (Acme). I can flag that as non-recurring and provide the amortized view for the appendix by Wed EOD.
2) Do you want the cost appendix to include per-model unit economics or just platform-level variance? I recommend platform-level + one model callout (GPT-small-quant) to show sensitivity.

I'll coordinate with finance and drop the amortized numbers into the Drive doc.

– Karthik
Senior Director, Finance

On Mon, Oct 12, 2026 at 11:02 AM Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai> wrote:
> thanks — yes, platform-level plus one model callout is perfect. Appreciate the quick turnaround.
>
> -L

-----Original Message-----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekly leadership roundup — priorities, QBR playbook, and blockers

Laura / team —

Uploaded QBR_playbook_draft_v1.pptx to Drive (link above). Notes:
- Slides 3–5: escalation ladder + contact matrix (please check primary/secondary contacts).
- Slides 6–7: customer-facing fallback script and the stubbed demo sequence. I kept the language simple for exec audience.
- Slide 8: decision checkpoints (canary -> canary rollback -> circuit-breaker fallback).

Two asks from my side:
1) Marketing: can we get a one-line customer impact stat for the fallback slide (e.g., "expected 60% reduction in time-to-first-complete-response"), or should I use internal bench numbers?
2) SRE: Markus, is the short incident blurb confirmed? If not, I put a placeholder and will update once you share the ETA.

Attachment (uploaded): QBR_playbook_draft_v1.pptx (pptx, 12 slides, draft)

— Marissa
Director, Product & GTM

On Wed, Oct 14, 2026 at 15:22:00 -0700 Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Laura / team —
>
> Postmortem ETA: EOD Thu 10/15. Root cause is narrowed to a misrouted KV cache invalidation in the multi-region router; we have a mitigation (circuit-breaker) ready for canary tomorrow.
>
> I'll add a 3–4 line blurb suitable for the risk register and drop it into the Drive folder.
>
> — Markus
> Senior Engineering Manager, SRE

On Wed, Oct 14, 2026 at 16:05:00 -0700 Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai> wrote:
> +1 on the playbook — I'll attend the dry run and will be ready to speak to the ops cadence.
>
> Hannah
> SVP, People & Strategy
